title: The debit-card decline is broad-based across banks
estimate: 20 of 20 banks fell (p = 9.5e-07); excluding SBI: -28.6% a year [95% CI -33.0%, -23.9%]
consistency: 37 of the 37 year-on-year changes were below zero
test: Two parts. (1) Sign test: annualised change in each bank's debit-card payments, FY2022-23 to FY2025-26, for the 20 largest issuers in FY2022-23; supported if one-sided binomial p < 0.05. (2) Drift test on all other banks' combined monthly debit payments (excluding SBI), Newey-West (12-lag) SE.

title: Public-sector banks' debit use per card falls faster
consistency: 37 of the 37 year-on-year monthly changes were above zero
test: Mean of [Δ12 ln(PSB payments per card) − Δ12 ln(private payments per card)]. Mean year-on-year log change, Newey-West (12-lag) standard errors, 37 months Mar 2023–Mar 2026. Supported if the 95% interval is below zero.

title: Credit-card payments concentrate in private banks
consistency: 21 of the 37 year-on-year monthly changes were above zero
test: Mean of Δ12 log-odds(private-bank share of credit-card payments). Mean year-on-year log change, Newey-West (12-lag) standard errors, 37 months Mar 2023–Mar 2026. Supported if the 95% interval is above zero.

title: Banks whose customers adopt UPI faster lose debit use faster
test: Cross-section of banks present in both RBI bank-wise card data and NPCI's top-50 UPI member list in every month of FY2022-23 and FY2025-26. OLS with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) SE. Supported if b < 0 with the 95% interval below zero.
data: RBI Bank-wise ATM/PoS/Card Statistics (monthly, Mar 2022–Mar 2026); NPCI UPI ecosystem statistics: Top 50 member banks (volume)

title: The two leading apps gain share
consistency: 26 of the 39 year-on-year monthly changes were above zero
test: Mean of Δ12 log-odds(PhonePe + Google Pay share of UPI volume). Mean year-on-year log change, Newey-West (12-lag) standard errors, 39 months Jan 2023–Mar 2026. Supported if the 95% interval is above zero.
data: NPCI UPI ecosystem statistics: UPI Applications

title: Paytm's lost share went to the two leaders
estimate: Level shift δ = -0.485 (-38.4%) [95% CI -0.648, -0.323]; leaders captured 89% of Paytm's lost share
test: (1) Known-date break in ln(Paytm share) at Feb 2024 with separate pre/post trends; Newey-West (12-lag) SE; supported if the level shift δ < 0 with its 95% interval below zero. (2) Share capture = gain in leaders' share ÷ loss in Paytm's share, Nov 2023–Jan 2024 average vs Apr–Jun 2024 average; supported if above 0.5.
data: NPCI UPI ecosystem statistics: UPI Applications

title: Smaller apps grow their share
consistency: 27 of the 39 year-on-year monthly changes were above zero
test: Mean of Δ12 log-odds(share of apps outside the top 3). Mean year-on-year log change, Newey-West (12-lag) standard errors, 39 months Jan 2023–Mar 2026. Supported if the 95% interval is above zero.
data: NPCI UPI ecosystem statistics: UPI Applications

title: Digital payments spread beyond the leading states
consistency: 13 of the 13 year-on-year quarterly changes were below zero
test: Mean of Δ4 log-odds(top-5 states' share of PhonePe transactions). Mean year-on-year log change, Newey-West (4-lag) standard errors, 13 quarters Q1 2023–Q1 2026. Supported if the 95% interval is below zero.
data: PhonePe Pulse open data (CDLA-Permissive-2.0), state transaction counts by category

title: Merchant payments gain share in most states
estimate: 36 of 36 states rose (p = 1.5e-11); national +0.134 log points a year [95% CI +0.095, +0.172]
consistency: 13 of the 13 year-on-year quarterly changes were above zero
test: (1) Sign test across 36 states/UTs: merchant share of transactions in calendar 2025 vs 2022; supported if one-sided binomial p < 0.05. (2) National PhonePe merchant share: mean Δ4 log-odds, Newey-West (4-lag) SE, Q1 2023–Q1 2026.
data: PhonePe Pulse open data (CDLA-Permissive-2.0), state transaction counts by category

title: States with low merchant use catch up
test: Cross-section of 36 states/UTs: annualised change in log-odds merchant share, 2022–2025, on its 2022 level; OLS with HC1 SE. Supported if b < 0 with the 95% interval below zero.
data: PhonePe Pulse open data (CDLA-Permissive-2.0), state transaction counts by category
